summary.text: Robert J. "Rob" Wittman is the Republican U.S. Representative for Virginia's 1st District, first elected in a 2007 special election after about 26 years in Virginia state government and service in local and state office. He sits on the House Armed Services and Natural Resources Committees, and his official biography emphasizes military and veterans' issues, the Chesapeake Bay, infrastructure and rural broadband.

paragraphs.text: Wittman was born in Washington, D.C., in 1959. According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he grew up in Henrico County, where his mother taught school and his father had served in the Army in World War II.

He earned a bachelor's degree in biology from Virginia Tech in 1981, a master's degree in health policy and administration from the University of North Carolina in 1990, and a Ph.D. in public policy and administration from Virginia Commonwealth University in 2002.

Before Congress he spent 26 years in Virginia state government, first as an environmental health specialist for local health departments in the Northern Neck and Middle Peninsula and later as field director of the Virginia Health Department's Division of Shellfish Sanitation.
Wittman won his first race in 1986, for the Montross Town Council, on which he served for 10 years, four of them as mayor.
He was elected to the Westmoreland County Board of Supervisors in 1995 and became its chairman in 2003.
In 2005 he was elected to the Virginia House of Delegates from the 99th District and served until his election to the U.S. House in 2007.

Wittman has represented Virginia's 1st District since 2007. His official biography lists him as vice chairman of the House Armed Services Committee and chairman of its Tactical Air and Land Forces Subcommittee, as a member of the Natural Resources Committee and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, and as co-chair of the Congressional Shipbuilding Caucus and the Chesapeake Bay Watershed Caucus.
The biography says his Serving Rural America Act served as a model for the NTIA Broadband Infrastructure Program and that he serves on the U.S. Naval Academy's Board of Visitors.
According to his Ballotpedia survey, he and his wife, Kathryn, have lived in Montross since 1985 and have two children and six grandchildren.
